program_name: Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering (Italian: Ingegneria elettronica e dell'informazione; German: Elektro- und Informationstechnik)
teaching_language: Trilingual. The official teaching languages of the programme are German, Italian and English, and courses are taught in all three. unibz does not publish a fixed percentage weighting per language for this programme, and the language of individual courses can change from year to year, so the exact split between EN/IT/DE is not officially quantified. [uncertain] What is officially fixed instead is the position-based language rule: a candidate must hold B2 in whichever of the three is their strongest language and B1 in a second one, and must reach B1 in the third language to be allowed to sit curricular exams held in that language. The study plan additionally contains a 3 CP 'Specialized language (Italian, German or English)' course.
campus: NOI Techpark, Bozen-Bolzano (Italy). The Faculty of Engineering is located at the NOI Techpark science and technology park in Bolzano, not at the main Universitatsplatz/piazza Universita campus.
degree_class: L-8 (Ingegneria dell'informazione / Information Engineering). Confirmed in both the 2026/27 admission-information PDF and the 2026/27 brochure.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes - actively offered and recruiting for 2026/27. All three application sessions ran: Early Bird and Late are closed with signed ranking lists published, and the Additional Application Session (EU citizens only) is explicitly listed as 'Application possible' for this programme and is open 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026, i.e. still open as of the verification date 2026-08-29. Teaching starts with Freshers Days 28-29/09/2026 and first-semester classes on 28/09/2026.
is_new_programme: No. This is an established programme, not a new 2026/27 launch. The unibz Study Guide publishes separate study plans for cohorts enroled from 2022/23, 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26, which places the first intake at academic year 2022/23. The genuinely new element for 2026/27 is not the programme but the admission route: the signed ranking-list decree states that from a.y. 2026/27 the national TOLC-I / CENT-S tests may be used for admission in addition to the unibz admission exam.
majors_tracks_study_plans: None. The programme has a single, undifferentiated study plan with no majors, tracks, curricula or dual-study variant (unlike the sister Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering, which offers five study plans plus a 4-year dual-study option). Structure: 3 years, 180 ECTS. Year 1 covers Linear Algebra (6), Mathematical Analysis I (9), Fundamentals of Programming I+II (6+5), Economics and Management (6), Mathematical Analysis II (9), Ubiquitous Sensing and Computing (3+5), Physics I (7), Specialized language (3). Year 2 covers Electronic Materials and Devices (5+9), Physics II (7), Data Structures and Algorithms (6), Probability Theory and Statistics (6), Basics of Electronics (9), Operating Systems and Networking (6), Fundamentals of Systems and Control incl. Lab (6+6). Year 3 covers Modern Control (9), Electronic Circuits and Systems - Analog Electronics + Digital Circuits and Systems (6+6), Robot Control (6), Computer Architecture (6), Machine Learning (9), two Free Choice courses (6+6), Internship (6) and Thesis (3).
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed. A candidate who speaks only English cannot satisfy the entry requirement, because admission demands B2 in a first language AND B1 in a second language chosen from German, Italian and English. English alone covers only the first-language slot; the applicant must additionally prove at least B1 in German or Italian before the application deadline or be excluded from the admission procedure outright. This is not a theoretical barrier: in the 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list, zero of the non-EU applicants living abroad were admitted and eight were excluded specifically for failing the language requirements, leaving the 2 non-EU places unfilled. An English-only applicant can realistically only enter by first obtaining a recognised B1 certificate in Italian or German, or by passing the unibz Language Centre B1 exam (note: the Language Centre does NOT offer language exams during the Additional Application Session). Once enroled, the third language must reach B1 by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2, and C1/B2/B2 is required to graduate.
admission_type: Restricted access (numerus clausus, fixed number of places) combined with a compulsory entry test. There is no open access, no interview, no portfolio and no motivation letter. Selection is purely test-based: applicants must pass through one of three accepted admission tests (unibz admission exam OR TOLC-I OR CENT-S), and are then ranked by normalised test score against the available places. Language requirements act as a hard pre-filter: applicants who cannot document the required levels are excluded from the procedure before ranking.
academic_requirements: A secondary school leaving certificate from the Italian system, or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school leaving certificate is considered equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education, and the applicant must have attended at least the final two years within that foreign school system (the PDF gives the Irish Leaving Certificate as an example: attending one year and obtaining the certificate is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain certificates, explicitly naming American high school diplomas and British and Greek certificates; such candidates are directed to apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). No subject-specific prerequisites, no minimum grade average and no ECTS/SSD credit requirements apply (those are master-level concepts). Under national rules a student may be simultaneously enroled in a maximum of 2 study programmes, provided the two do not belong to the same degree class (e.g. not L-18 plus L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of their course content. Language requirements must be met in addition to the academic qualification.

entry_exam_or_test.summary: Three mutually alternative tests are accepted; the candidate takes ONE of them. All assess mathematics plus a physics/science component. New for a.y. 2026/27: the national CISIA tests TOLC-I and CENT-S became acceptable alongside the in-house unibz exam.

options.name: unibz admission exam
options.format: Online, sat remotely on fixed dates set by unibz
options.languages: Available in German, Italian and English - the official mock test and the topic guidelines are published trilingually, so an English-speaking candidate can sit this test in English
preparation_materials: Mock Admission Test (trilingual, shared with the Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering): https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Engineering/Mock-Admission-Test-ENG.pdf
Topics Guidelines for the Admission Test: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Engineering/Topics-Admission-ENG.pdf
options.syllabus: Mathematics (secondary-school algebra and geometry: operations with real numbers including logarithms and exponentials, literal calculus, polynomials, equations and inequalities, analytic geometry in the plane, properties of plane and solid figures, areas and volumes, basic set theory); elementary probability (random events, independent events, conditional probability); elementary combinatorics (factorials, permutations, combinations); Physics (mechanics, thermodynamics and electromagnetism: fundamental physical quantities, units, inertia, Newton's laws, action-reaction, ideal gas equation of state, basic electrostatics and magnetostatics, Ohm's law); Chemistry (qualitative knowledge of atoms and molecules, chemical notation, periodic table, ions, definition of pH, acids and bases, basic chemical equations, acid-base reactions, redox reactions).

options.name: TOLC-I (CISIA)
options.format: Can be taken at ANY Italian university that offers it; at unibz it is administered in person on published dates. Registration and calendar are handled by CISIA, not unibz.
options.sections_counted_for_ranking: Mathematics and science only (the Logic, Verbal comprehension and English sections are not counted by unibz for this programme's ranking)
options.test_structure_reference: Per CISIA, TOLC-I consists of 50 questions in 4 sections - Mathematics (20 questions, 50 min), Logic (10, 20 min), Science (10, 20 min), Verbal comprehension (10, 20 min) - totalling 110 minutes, plus a separate 30-question English section in 15 minutes. Scoring on the main sections is +1 correct, 0 blank, -0.25 wrong; the English section carries no penalty. [uncertain] - this structural detail comes from CISIA rather than from unibz.it, and unibz only specifies which sections it counts.

options.name: CENT-S (CISIA)
options.format: Can be taken at any university offering it; at unibz administered in person on published dates. Registration via CISIA.
options.relevance_for_english_speakers: CENT-S is CISIA's English-language test for the scientific area, which makes it the natural route for a candidate who prefers to test in English. [uncertain] - the English-language framing and the 55-question / 110-minute five-section structure (Mathematics, Reasoning on texts and data, Biology, Chemistry, Physics) come from third-party CISIA-derived sources, not from unibz.it.

entry_exam_or_test.note: unibz states only 'TOLC I / CENT-S admission exam: available deadlines' in each session block and links out to the CISIA calendars, so the CISIA test dates are not fixed by unibz and must be checked on testcisia.it. Candidates must ensure their CISIA result is available to unibz by the relevant application deadline.

selection_scoring: Raw scoring is identical across the accepted tests: +1 point per correct answer, 0 points for an unanswered question, and -0.25 points for a wrong answer. The ranking is then built on the score obtained in the admission test 'appropriately normalised to the maximum score of each test', counting only the designated sections (unibz exam: mathematics and physics/chemistry; TOLC-I: mathematics and science; CENT-S: mathematics and physics). This normalisation is what makes the three routes comparable within one ranking list. Ties are broken in favour of the younger candidate. No minimum pass mark or qualifying threshold is published for this programme - candidates are simply ranked and the top N take the available places, with the remainder placed on a waiting list. [uncertain] - the absence of a minimum threshold is inferred from the fact that neither the admission-information PDF nor the signed ranking-list decrees state one; scoring below 30% does not exclude a candidate but triggers OFA. Actual scores are not published in the ranking lists (only Applicant IDs), so no historical cut-off score can be quoted. Observed competitiveness for 2026/27 is low: Early Bird admitted exactly 20 with only 3 candidates on the waiting list (positions 21-23), and the Late session admitted 13 with no waiting list at all.
bonus_points: None. No bonus points of any kind apply to this programme - there is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to the Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation), and no credit for work experience or prior qualifications. The ranking is determined exclusively by the normalised admission-test score, with age as the sole tie-breaker.
portfolio_and_materials: None required. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter and no CV form part of this admission procedure, and consequently no format or size limits apply. This is a purely test-based engineering admission, in contrast to the Design and Art or Social Education bachelors.
interview: No. There is no interview stage at any point in the admission procedure for this programme, and no interview dates are published.
conditional_admission: Yes, applicants who have not yet completed secondary school may apply. The admission-information PDF states that if the applicant gained their qualification abroad and is 'not yet in possession of the diploma', the diploma must be uploaded upon enrolment rather than at application. Admission for non-EU citizens living abroad is additionally granted 'with reservation' (con riserva / mit Vorbehalt) in the ranking lists: the reservation is lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. A candidate admitted without a valid access qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. Financial consequence: paying the first instalment normally forfeits any refund, but a refund IS granted in exactly two cases - if the candidate fails their secondary school final exam (maturita/Abitur), or if a non-EU candidate living abroad fails to obtain the documents required for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. Note that the master-level rule of a minimum 120 (or 140) ECTS for conditional admission does not apply at bachelor level.
ofa_rules: OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) applies to this programme and is score-triggered, not subject-triggered. If an applicant obtains a percentage less than or equal to 30% of the maximum achievable score in the relevant sections of the admission exam, they are assigned OFA to be fulfilled during the first year. A preparatory course is organised in the weeks preceding the start of the first semester so students can sit the OFA remedial test (this aligns with the Mathematics pre-course, 21/09 - 09/10/2026). The OFA test must be passed within the first academic year and is an essential requirement for taking curricular exams in later years: if the student does not pass it, they are barred from sitting any exams scheduled for the second and third year of the programme. This is stricter and more consequential than the OFA regime at the Economics faculty, where OFA follows a compulsory mathematics test.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and language proficiency is a hard admission filter - the PDF is explicit that failing it means 'you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. Requirements are defined by POSITION (first/second/third strongest language), not by which specific language it is. To gain admission: B2 in the first language and B1 in the second; no level is required in the third, though a B1 there is the minimum for sitting curricular exams held in that language. Preference is given to candidates with B2 in their second language. To graduate: C1 in the first language, B2 in the second and B2 in the third. CEFR levels apply throughout. The first language is defined as the one in which the candidate has the highest proficiency (B2 or C1); the third is the weakest, possibly absolute beginner. Certification is mandatory for the first and second language and recommended (from B1 up) for the third. Certificates from an Italian public institution require a self-declaration; those from a foreign public institution require an uploaded scan of the original. Candidates who cannot certify their third language and are admitted must take a placement test and are assigned a learning path; absolute beginners are advised to attend the three-week intensive course in September, because A1 beginner courses are offered ONLY in that pre-semester session and no longer during the academic year. Language Centre courses are free of charge, run as extensive courses (4 h/week) during semesters and intensive courses (8 h/week) between semesters, and target B1 by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2. Important caveat for the Additional Application Session: the Language Centre offers no language exams for that session, so applicants must arrive with an external certificate (unibz recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS for speed) and cannot attend the September intensive courses.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 | 2nd language: B1 | 3rd language: no level required. Preference in selection is given to candidates holding B2 in their second language. A B1 in the third language is the minimum needed to take curricular examinations conducted in that language. This B2/B1/none profile is the more permissive engineering-faculty pattern (identical to the Bachelor in Computer Science entry bar being B2/B1) and is markedly easier than the C1/B2 profile demanded by programmes such as the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance or the Master in Accounting and Finance. The signed ranking-list decrees restate the rule in binding form: admission requires 'adequate competences (level B2 CEFR in one and level B1 in another) of the three teaching languages (German, Italian, English)'.
exit_levels: 1st language: C1 | 2nd language: B2 | 3rd language: B2. These are graduation requirements, so they directly gate degree completion rather than admission. The third-language jump is the demanding part: a student admitted with no third-language knowledge at all must climb from zero to B2 during the degree, supported by free Language Centre courses targeting B1 by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations delivered in that language. The Language Centre's learning path is calibrated to deliver B1 by the end of the first year, so in practice a student starting from zero is expected to unlock third-language exams from the second year onwards. Failing to certify the third language at admission triggers a compulsory placement test after admission, which assigns the student to an appropriate learning path.

proof_pathways.summary: Four officially recognised ways to demonstrate proficiency, declared in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'.
pathways: 1. Main teaching language of the final year of high school, if German, Italian or English - recognised as C1. Ladin upper secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian. For foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter or document from the school stating it must also be uploaded.

2. A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English - recognised as C1. unibz graduates must upload their obtained certificates and/or declare that they passed Language Centre exams (B2, B2+ or C1). For foreign degrees, if the teaching language is not clearly stated, a letter from the university stating the medium of instruction is required.

3. A recognised language certificate from the official list (University Council Resolution 16/2026). If the certificate cannot be uploaded, it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.

4. Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, booked online through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams'. Only B1 and B2 level exams can be booked, and only one level per language per session (e.g. B1 German plus B2 Italian is allowed; B1 German plus B2 German is not). If an application is started outside a registration window, the candidate must return to the portal during one of the windows to register.
unibz_language_exam_dates_2026_27: Early Bird - exams (online) 2026-04-16/17 and 2026-04-20/21, registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08
Late Application - exams (online) 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26, registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15
Additional Application Session - NO Language Centre exams are offered; an external certificate is required
proof_pathways.special_case_bilingual_and_foreign_schoo: If CEFR levels for German, Italian or English are explicitly stated on the school leaving diploma and all four skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the second and/or third language. The diploma is uploaded under 'upload language certificates' for the respective language and the Language Centre decides on recognition.

certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 (published trilingually as 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants'). To be recognised, an international certificate must (1) include assessment of all four skills and be issued by the certification organisation itself, and (2) show a sufficient result in each skill as an overall grade, or provide the detailed per-skill assessment on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer. If no overall level is stated, the LOWEST level reached in any single sub-skill determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed. There is no compensation for failed parts and no averaging, unless the certification body itself provides for it. Certificates obtained as remote 'Home Edition' exams are NOT recognised, except for those explicitly flagged as such in the official list. Certificates covering single skills from different certification bodies are not accepted. Course attendance certificates, end-of-course tests, exams from private training providers and placement test results are not recognised. Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teachers are not recognised, and DAAD certificates are explicitly not recognised. Validity: international certificates must not be older than five years at the time of submission, counted generously as the whole calendar year from 1 January of the fifth preceding year. Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Official list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf

early_bird.note: Closes at noon local time. Open to EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment. Original wording: 'Application: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time)'.

late_application.note: Closes at noon local time. EU citizens only. Candidates excluded in the first session may re-apply here, and a test score already obtained remains valid if they re-apply.

additional_session.note: Closes at noon local time. EU citizens only, and offered only if places remain. CONFIRMED OPEN for this programme in 2026/27 - the official Additional Application Session page lists 'Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering (Application possible)'. Caveats specific to this session: no unibz Language Centre exams are offered, and admitted students cannot attend the September intensive language courses, so third-language beginners are strongly advised to acquire A1 before starting; A1 courses then restart mid-October 2026.

single_window.note: Closes at noon local time. Non-EU citizens living outside Italy have ONE application window only, coinciding with the Early Bird window; after that deadline it is not possible to apply at all. They are excluded from both the Late Application and the Additional Application Session, both of which are EU-only. This makes the Early Bird window the single hard gate for applicants from outside the EU, including applicants from Turkey who do not hold an Italian residence permit.

parity_of_treatment: Two groups are treated as equivalent to EU citizens for admission purposes. (1) Citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State. (2) Non-EU citizens holding a valid permit to stay in Italy under article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 - specifically a 'permesso di soggiorno' for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, or religious reasons. Such applicants apply directly to the University and must upload a copy of the valid permit; if the permit has expired, a renewal request must be attached. Critically, a permit to stay for STUDY reasons and a tourist visa do NOT qualify. The consequence of omission is automatic and severe: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin' - which for this programme means being pushed into the single Early Bird window competing for only 2 places. This third category is the decisive one for Turkish applicants already legally resident in Italy on a work or family permit, since it moves them from the 2-place non-EU pool into the 28-place EU pool and unlocks the Late and Additional sessions.

places_quotas.additional_session_places: Not published as a fixed number; the Faculty opens the session only if places remain after the first two rounds. [uncertain]
places_quotas.note: The brochure's headline figure 'Places available: 28 EU + 2 Non-EU' is the sum of the two EU sub-quotas (20 + 8), not a third separate number - the admission-information PDF and the programme page both itemise it as Early Bird 20 / Late 8. Unfilled Early Bird places roll forward: 'any remaining places of the early bird application will be offered in the late application', which is visible in the 2026/27 outcome where the Late session admitted 13 candidates against a nominal 8 places.
places_quotas.observed_2026_27_outcome: Early Bird: 20 EU admitted (full), 3 on the waiting list (ranks 21-23), 6 excluded for not sitting the test despite meeting language requirements, 5 excluded for failing language requirements; 0 of 2 non-EU places filled, with 8 non-EU applicants excluded for failing language requirements. Late: 13 EU admitted, no waiting list, 1 excluded for not sitting the test, 4 excluded for language requirements. Net signal: the programme is not academically competitive, and the binding constraint is the language requirement rather than the test score.

early_bird.waiting_list_activation: Candidates from rank 21 onward are contacted by e-mail from 2026-06-08 if admitted candidates fail to secure their place in time

late_application.enrolment_window: From publication of the ranking list until 2026-08-06 (noon local time)

additional_session.enrolment_window: From publication of the ranking list until 2026-09-25 (noon local time)

ranking_and_enrolment_dates.rules: Paying the first instalment secures the place but does NOT confer student status - that is acquired only by completing enrolment. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of 2 programmes by paying the instalment twice. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline results in automatic forfeiture and the place passes to the next candidate in the ranking. Enrolling early is recommended so that incomplete documents can be corrected before the deadline. Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Administrative Court of Bolzano within 60 days of notification or publication.

programme_specific_dates.tolc_i_and_cent_s: No unibz-fixed dates; candidates use the CISIA calendars (testcisia.it). At unibz these tests are administered in person on dates listed in the CISIA calendar.
programme_specific_dates.intensive_language_courses: 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-18, Monday to Friday, 6 h/day (not available to Additional Session entrants)
programme_specific_dates.mathematics_pre_course: 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-09 (also the window for OFA remedial preparation)
programme_specific_dates.a1_language_courses_for_additional_sessi: From mid-October 2026; standard path to B1 runs October 2026 to September 2027

required_documents: Valid ID card or passport, front and back - an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document causes exclusion from the admission procedure

Completed online application form submitted through the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup) by the deadline; once sent it cannot be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are disregarded

Language certificates or self-declarations proving the required levels, uploaded under 'upload language certificates' (mandatory for 1st and 2nd language, recommended from B1 for the 3rd); alternatively registration for unibz Language Centre exams under 'enrol for language exams'
Diploma of the qualification, if gained abroad - uploaded at application, or at enrolment if not yet in possession
For applicants claiming parity of treatment: a copy of the valid Italian permit to stay (or a renewal request if expired) - omitting this reclassifies the applicant as non-EU living abroad

At enrolment with a foreign secondary school qualification: the secondary school diploma, plus an official Italian translation (not required for diplomas issued in German or English), plus the applicable recognition statements (see credential_recognition)
For non-EU citizens living abroad: mandatory pre-enrolment on the Universitaly portal after paying the first instalment, and later the residence permit handed in at the Student Office
required_documents_note: No structured study-career Excel template is required for this programme. That mandatory upload belongs to unibz master-level admissions, where prior ECTS/SSD credits must be itemised; bachelor admission has no equivalent requirement. [uncertain] - stated as absent because neither the admission-information PDF nor the programme page mentions it anywhere in the bachelor document list.
application_fee: EUR 50, charged ONLY to non-EU citizens living abroad. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total EUR 1,200 per academic year, paid in two instalments of EUR 600. The 1st instalment (EUR 600) includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp and is the payment that secures an admitted place by the session deadline. The 2nd instalment (EUR 600) must be paid by March of the following year; late payment incurs a fine, and unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or programme. No refund is due on dropping out, interrupting studies or being excluded - the only refund cases are failing the secondary school final exam or, for non-EU applicants abroad, failing to obtain enrolment documents from the Italian authorities. Full exemption is granted to students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or more (certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and to foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Students receiving a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of tuition fees. Official fees page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/
scholarships_grants: The principal instrument is the provincial income-based study grant administered by the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario (Office for the Right to University Study) of the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, worth between EUR 1,680 and EUR 6,960 per year depending on income; recipients also receive a refund of their tuition fees. Eligibility is residence-gated, which is the decisive constraint for international students: applicants must have one year of regular, uninterrupted residence in South Tyrol, and non-EU students qualify only if they hold a long-term residence permit or have completed at least one uninterrupted year of residence in South Tyrol. In practice this means a non-EU student arriving from abroad cannot access the provincial grant in their first year. No programme-specific scholarship is attached to this degree (unlike the Bachelor in Food and Enogastronomy Sciences, which has a dedicated Meran-Merano municipal scholarship). Merit-based support and further study grants are described on the Study Guide page. Cost-of-living context published by unibz: the sudtirolmobil U26 Pass costs EUR 150 per year for students under 26 and covers all South Tyrol public transport plus regional trains to Trento. [uncertain] - grant amounts and thresholds are set annually by the Province and the 2026/27 figures may be revised; the EUR 1,680-6,960 range is the figure currently published by unibz. Source: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants
credential_recognition: Required at enrolment for holders of a foreign secondary school qualification, in three tiers determined by the country of origin. In all three cases the applicant uploads the secondary school diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English). (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and holders of the International Baccalaureate or European Baccalaureate: additionally a Statement of Correspondence downloaded from ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database - Italy. (b) Non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention: additionally a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA (Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence). (c) Non-EU countries that are NOT signatories to the Lisbon Convention: a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so Turkish applicants fall under tier (b) and need ARDI Correspondence plus CIMEA Verification. unibz performs its own checks and reserves the right to request additional documents in case of doubt; a candidate found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. The bachelor-level rule requires no proof of 180 ECTS - that applies to master admission.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window (02/03 - 28/04/2026) paying the EUR 50 non-refundable application fee; if admitted per the ranking list, secure the place by paying the first instalment; then start the visa application on the Universitaly portal. Pre-enrolment on Universitaly is MANDATORY - without it enrolment is not permitted - and only ONE study programme may be selected there, so the choice is committing. Admission is granted with reservation, lifted only when the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz; the Italian authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa. Financial means: unibz advises at least EUR 800 per month for living costs in the Bozen-Bolzano area (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) plus health insurance and visa expenses, indicating a total of at least EUR 36,000 for a bachelor programme (versus EUR 24,000 for a master). On arrival, the residence permit application must be lodged within 8 working days: collect the application kit from the Post Office, book an appointment with Student Support who help complete the form, check documents and issue the enrolment confirmation. Permit costs comprise a EUR 16 duty stamp, EUR 30 for the insured envelope, EUR 30 for the electronic permit and a further EUR 40 for stays over 90 days up to one year. Once issued, the permesso di soggiorno must be handed in at the Student Office in person or by e-mail; it also allows Schengen travel for up to 90 days and re-entry to Italy while valid. Refund protection: a non-EU applicant who pays but cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities is entitled to a refund. [uncertain] - the 20 hours/week student work limit is Italian national law rather than a unibz-published figure and was not restated on the unibz pages consulted.

uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are the 2026/27 cycle. The primary source PDF carries 'Latest update: 29.07.2026' and states 'Subject to change'. Verified 2026-08-29.

Timing caveat: at the verification date the Early Bird and Late sessions were already closed with signed ranking lists published, and only the Additional Application Session (EU citizens only, closing 2026-09-04) remained open. Any Turkish or other non-EU applicant living abroad has already missed the 2026/27 cycle entirely and must target 2027/28.

Apparent conflict resolved: the brochure headline '28 EU + 2 Non-EU' initially looks inconsistent with the PDF's '20 / 8 / 2', but 28 is simply the EU total (20 Early Bird + 8 Late). Both the admission PDF and the live programme page were checked against the raw HTML to confirm 20 / 8 / 2.

Teaching-language weighting: unibz publishes no percentage split of EN/IT/DE teaching for this programme, and course languages can vary by year and by lecturer, so 'trilingual' cannot be quantified from official sources.

No numeric admission cut-off exists in the public record: the signed ranking lists publish Applicant IDs only, never scores, so competitiveness can only be inferred from admitted-versus-waitlisted counts (Early Bird 20 admitted + 3 waitlisted; Late 13 admitted + no waitlist).

No minimum qualifying score is published for this programme. Scoring at or below 30% does not exclude a candidate; it triggers OFA. The inference that no exclusion threshold exists rests on the silence of both the admission PDF and the ranking decrees.
Additional Application Session place count is not published as a number - the Faculty opens it only where places remain, so the size of the remaining pool is unknown.

Shared faculty documents: the linked Mock Admission Test and Topics Guidelines PDFs are headed 'Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering'. The mock test explicitly also names 'Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering' in its trilingual header, so it is genuinely shared; the Topics PDF names only Industrial and Mechanical Engineering in its heading despite being linked from this programme's page, so its syllabus is taken as applicable but the heading is a documentation inconsistency on unibz's side.

TOLC-I and CENT-S structural details (question counts, durations, section names, CENT-S being CISIA's English-language scientific test) come from CISIA and CISIA-derived third-party sources, not from unibz.it, which specifies only which sections it counts and links to the CISIA calendars. These fall outside the outline's unibz.it-only source restriction and are flagged inline.
Provincial study-grant amounts (EUR 1,680-6,960) are set annually by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano; the figure is the one currently published by unibz but may be revised for 2026/27.
The 20 hours/week student work limit noted in the field brief is Italian national immigration law and was not restated on any unibz page consulted for this programme.
No official English-language Faculty of Engineering admission regulation URL could be located; the ranking decrees cite a 'Regolamento di ammissione' art. 14 without linking it.

Accessibility judgement: 'effectively-closed' for English-only candidates is a derived assessment, not an official unibz label. It follows from the binding B2+B1 two-language rule plus the observed 2026/27 outcome in which every non-EU applicant was excluded on language grounds.
